toc: true

The wireless rack holds the **Sennheiser EM-XSW 2 receivers**. Everything in the rack is **numbered**, and the numbers match:

| Number on… | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Bodypack** (SK-XSW) | The transmitter the performer wears |
| **Receiver** (EM-XSW 2) | The box in the rack with two antennas |
| **XLR cable** | Runs from that receiver to the snake |
| **Power adapter** | Powers that receiver. All of them plug into one power strip |

**The one rule: same number goes with same number.** Pack 3 → receiver 3 → XLR 3 → adapter 3.

## 1. Before you lift

- [ ] Count the bodypacks. Every pack in the bag should have a receiver with the same number in the rack.
- [ ] Put fresh **AA batteries** in each pack (or check they're charged).
- [ ] Check that the power strip is **switched off** and its plug is pulled.

## 2. Move the rack

1. Tuck the loose XLR cables and the power strip's lead inside the rack so nothing drags on the floor.
2. Lift with **two people**, one on each side, using the **handles**. Never lift by an antenna or a cable.
3. Put it down **flat, on a table or the floor**, near the stage end of the snake.
4. Point the **antennas up**, angled slightly left and right (Sennheiser manual p. 42). Don't put anything on top of the rack.
5. Keep the rack where it can "see" the stage, so there's no wall or metal cabinet between the rack and the performers.

## 3. Power

1. Check that each **power adapter** goes into the **receiver with its number**. Push each one in firmly.
2. Plug the power strip into the wall. Use a wall socket, not another power strip.
3. Switch the power strip **on**.
4. Switch on each receiver.

## 4. XLR into the snake

The **snake** is the thick cable with a box of numbered XLR sockets on the stage end. Its other end goes to the X32.

1. **Mute the X32 first** (or pull the main fader down), so the plugging doesn't pop through the speakers.
2. Plug each receiver's **XLR cable** into the **snake socket with the same number**: XLR 1 → snake 1, XLR 2 → snake 2, and so on.
3. Push until it **clicks**. To unplug later, press the tab and then pull.
4. If a snake socket is already in use (say drums are on 1–4), use the next free sockets. **Write down which receiver went in which
   socket** on masking tape on the rack, and tell whoever is at the desk.

<!-- Our snake socket N = X32 input N? Not checked: confirm on the desk and fix this line. -->
On the X32, **snake socket N is channel N** (unless someone changed the routing). Wireless 1 shows up on channel 1, and so on.

## 5. At the X32

1. Turn on **phantom power (+48V)** on the wireless channels only if the desk usually has it on there. The receivers don't need it,
   and it does them no harm, but leave it alone if you're unsure.
2. Switch on **one bodypack at a time**. Talk into its mic.
3. Look at the meter on the channel with **that pack's number**. It should move.
4. Set the **gain** so your normal talking voice reaches about the middle of the meter, never into red.
   See [gain](../lessons/live-gain.qmd).
5. Bring up the fader. Then do the next pack.

## If something's wrong

| What you see | Try this |
|---|---|
| Receiver screen is dark | Is the power strip on? Is the adapter pushed in? Is it in the right number? |
| Receiver on, meter on the X32 doesn't move | Check the XLR at both ends (it must click). Is it in the right snake socket? Is the X32 channel muted? |
| Sound comes up on the wrong channel | The XLR is in the wrong snake socket, or the pack is in the wrong person's hands. Match the numbers again |
| You hear one pack on two channels | Two receivers are on frequencies that are too close: [fix it here](sennheiser-xsw.qmd) |
| Crackle or dropouts | Change the pack batteries. Point the antennas up. Move the rack so it can see the stage |

## Packing up

1. Pull the faders down or mute the wireless channels.
2. Switch off the bodypacks and **take their batteries out**.
3. Switch the power strip off, then unplug it from the wall.
4. Unplug the XLRs from the snake (press the tab). Coil each cable and tuck it into the rack, but **leave it plugged into its receiver**.
5. Carry the rack back with two people.
